title: Build and verify Crystal + Anchor Combat Optimizer for Minecraft 26.1.2
objective: Implement the approved fully client-side Fabric 26.1.2 combat optimizer that discovers and executes vanilla-valid end-crystal and respawn-anchor kill sequences using exact sequential damage simulation, bounded beam search, observable-only opponent intelligence, legal packet dependencies, adaptive risk, real rotations, and server reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: The repository contains a complete client-side Fabric project targeting exactly Minecraft 26.1.2 and Java 25 with pinned Fabric Loader, Loom, and Fabric API versions
GitHub Actions builds the project on Java 25 and runs deterministic unit tests plus configured Fabric GameTests
Hurt-window, armor/effect, absorption, totem, crystal, anchor, and sequential explosion behavior are implemented from 26.1.2 source-backed mechanics with no damage fudge factors
The planner uses bounded rolling-horizon beam search over primitive legal state transitions rather than hard-coded combos or a greedy highest-damage loop

Critical execution distinguishes zero-feedback action chains from genuine server-feedback boundaries and never fabricates entity IDs, movement, reach, rotations, inventory state, hidden opponent slots, or server tick phase
Opponent intelligence uses every legitimate client-visible equipment, pickup, consumption, pop, and timing signal while preserving exact, derived, and estimated uncertainty categories

Adaptive target/risk logic is kill-opportunity-first with threat weighting, opportunistic setup, no automatic movement, adaptive real rotations, and hotbar-first automatic restocking with the offhand reserved for future AutoTotem coordination
Runtime reconciliation invalidates stale plans against server-observed state and records simulator mismatches instead of compensating with magic constants
Every claimed progressive-damage, pop-lock, terrain/exposure, timing, or prepared-anchor optimization has a deterministic or differential regression test before live execution uses it
The normal UI stays compact while developer diagnostics can explain selected lines, damage deltas, confidence, packet dependencies, rejection reasons, and combat traces
The final build, test results, CI evidence, and any runtime-verification limitations are documented honestly
